transcript:
Header: 2025-12-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lily (CTO - Cobalt), Evan (Platform), Sara (Devops)

Summary (auto): finalization of cutover plan, runbook owners, smoke-test scope, security checklist.

00:00 Maya: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run 40 minutes. Quick agenda: canary numbers, smoke tests, rollback play, and security gating.
00:18 Lily: Yep, thanks. We've got the execs breathing down us for a week-of-launch window so want to make sure the safety gates are airtight.
00:26 Diego: Great, I'll start with canary. We propose staged traffic: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over four windows with 30m observation each, thresholds set on p95 latency and 5xx rate. If p95 increases >20% or 5xx >0.5% we'll stop.
00:49 Evan: Quick q, are those thresholds absolute or relative vs baseline? Our baseline for p95 is 220ms.
00:57 Diego: They're relative to baseline — so a 20% uptick over baseline. We also look at token cost delta and model output divergence for quality regressions.
01:12 Sara: For rollback, do we just cut traffic back to hosted variant or spin up previous model version? Our infra prefers traffic steering rather than new provisioning.
01:23 Diego: We recommend traffic steering to the previous model variant that's kept warm — Redwood can pin the older quantization profile and route back. That avoids cold-starts.
01:33 Lily: Okay, pinning sounds fine, but we need to document warm-up behavior. If the KV cache is invalidated, latency will spike.
01:42 Diego: noted — we'll include KV/prefix cache notes. Also canary will enable prefix cache warm-up for the target cohort.

05:02 Maya: Security gating — Lily, what do you need from Redwood to sign off? SOC2, KMS integration notes, audit log retention?
05:12 Lily: Yep, main asks: SOC2 attestation, KMS/HSM flow for customer keys, SSO via SAML, and retention windows for request and response logs. We can't keep raw PHI beyond 30 days.
05:28 Maya: We will send the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide. Redwood supports envelope encryption and HSM via our KMS plugin — Diego, correct?
05:36 Diego: Correct. We also support field-level redaction when at-rest retention must be reduced, and we can route logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies.
05:46 Evan: For private deployment — will audit logs show per-request token counts? We need that for cost allocation.
05:52 Diego: Yes we emit token and latency metadata per request in the trace, and the Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns.

10:10 Sara: Back to canary specifics — what's the smoke-test corpus? We can't test with live PHI.
10:17 Maya: Good call. We suggest a synthetic set plus redacted production prompts. The plan in brief: 5k synthetic prompts that mimic peak tokens distribution, 1k redacted prod prompts for quality checks, run both at each canary stage.
10:33 Lily: Who's responsible for generating the synthetic set?
10:36 Sara: I can generate the redacted set; synthetic we'll need Redwood's guidance on token distribution.
10:43 Diego: I'll attach a sample generator script and recommend distribution: 60% short (<32 tokens), 30% mid (32-128), 10% long (128-512). That should exercise batching and kernel selection.

15:05 Evan: Observability — we need dashboards. Can Redwood push a prebuilt Grafana dashboard or do we use the Console?
15:13 Maya: There's a Console dashboard but we can also export a JSON Grafana dashboard. We'll include alerts for p95, 5xx, token delta, and output regression rate.
15:23 Lily: Output regression how do you compute that?
15:26 Diego: We run a diff metric on embeddings and a heuristic on factuality for a labeled subset. It's not perfect but it catches systemic regressions early. We'll surface a regression score and examples.

20:02 Sara: I want to call out network cutover. We'll need a maintenance window and DNS TTL prep. If we change edge routing, some users may hit old endpoint for TTL seconds.
20:12 Evan: We'll set TTL to 60s prior to switch. Also, will Redwood support the fail-open path if peering is delayed?
20:20 Maya: We recommend two options: 1) fallback to hosted Redwood for a small percentage of traffic (cost tradeoff) or 2) return 503 early to force client backoff. Generally option 1 keeps UX smoother.
20:33 Lily: We prefer a smoother UX, even if it's slightly higher cost.

20:38 Diego: OK, we'll provision fallback routes and quantify the cost delta in the runbook.

25:00 Maya: Let's talk runbook ownership. Who will be primary and who is secondary for the cutover?
25:06 Lily: CTO approves, but Sara will be primary runbook executor with Evan as platform backup.
25:12 Maya: Redwood will be on-call during the safety window: Diego primary, Maya backup. We'll join the war-room Slack channel.

30:14 Diego: Rollback triggers (explicit): p95 >20% for 2 consecutive windows OR 5xx >0.5% OR regression score >0.15. Also a manual abort if stakeholder flags output quality. Those numbers are configurable — we wanted Cobalt to confirm.
30:34 Lily: Those thresholds look reasonable. Can we add a bursty traffic detector so we don't false-trigger on a sporadic surge?
30:42 Diego: We'll use a moving median and exclude outliers beyond 99th percentile spike. We'll add that to the monitoring rules.

34:00 Sara: Smoke-test automation: do you have a harness we can run from our infra or do we invoke Redwood's harness?
34:08 Diego: Both — we can provide a lightweight runner that hits your test endpoint using your credentials. We'll also run an internal parallel run to compare outputs.
34:18 Sara: Good. We'll want logs uploaded to our S3 and a prebuilt parser to extract latency histograms.
34:24 Diego: We'll provide the parser.

38:05 Maya: Any open concerns?
38:10 Lily: A minor one — data residency for EU users. Is the model pinned to a region?
38:16 Diego: We can pin serving region; for hybrid we can route EU traffic to our EU region and keep logs in region via S3 bucket. Will document cross-region failovers.
38:27 Lily: Okay.

40:00 Maya: Recap: Redwood to deliver canary config, Grafana JSON, runbook with rollback triggers and cost delta by 2025-12-22. Cobalt to provision VPC peering and run smoke tests by 2025-12-26. Safety window: 2025-12-29, 2 hours. Next sync if needed after smoke results.
40:20 Evan: We'll open a Jira and link it to the CRM deal.
40:28 Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with links in email.
40:34 Lily: Thanks, bye.
